newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks continue winning streak at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks continue winning streak at close.

text.p: Argentine stocks recorded their fourth consecutive five-year high at the close Tuesday, fuelled by a surge in the Dow and heavy buying in local telephone stocks, dealers said.

"Besides the context of stability provided by U.S. long bond yields, the bolsa today searched for new highs driven by the telephone sector which was lagging behind recent gains in the market," said Jose Napoli at brokers Ignoto y Napoli.
The blue-chip MerVal index tacked on 0.6 percent to 846.33, while Telefonica and Telecom jumped 5.3 percent and 3.7 percent, respectively.

"There's talk a U.S. telecommunications giant is eyeing business opportunies here, and also the courts are expected to rule in favor of the controversial telephone tariff reform decreed earlier this year. Furthermore, the local telephone companies are due to pay cash dividends soon," one dealer said.
Traders noted the MerVal was keen on reaching the psychological target of 850 after Wednesday's Independence Day holiday, and then would probably stay rangebound.
Floor volume eased to 33.1 million pesos Tuesday from 36.6 million Monday, while over-the-counter turnover remained hefty at 139.5 million pesos against 152.5 million Monday.
The broad market index closed up 1.6 percent, with winners pounding losers 43 to 25 and 24 issues closing unchanged.

Another strong MerVal gainer was holding company Garovaglio, which rose 3.5 percent after announcing the purchase Monday of a 70 percent stake in leading local meat processor and exporter Compania Elaboradora de Productos Alimenticios.
Worst main-tier performers were construction stock Polledo and oil company Astra, which fell 4.5 percent and 2.7 percent, respectively.
